tests.description: Verifies the player moves forward with W and jumps with Space, landing back on the ground.
tests.name: Player walks and jumps
source: const walkDist = Math.hypot(afterWalk.centerX - startX, afterWalk.centerY - startY);
harness.assert(walkDist > 50, 'Player moved forward while holding W (moved ' + walkDist.toFixed(1) + 'px).');
harness.assert(afterWalk.behaviors.PhysicsCharacter3D.state.IsOnFloor === true, 'Player is still on the ground after walking.');
const leftGround = await harness.stepUntil(() => getPlayer().behaviors.PhysicsCharacter3D.state.IsOnFloor === false, { maxFrames: 30 });
harness.assert(leftGround, 'Player left the ground after pressing Space (jump).');
const landed = await harness.stepUntil(() => getPlayer().behaviors.PhysicsCharacter3D.state.IsOnFloor === true, { maxFrames: 120 });
harness.assert(landed, 'Player landed back on the ground after jumping.');

tests.description: Player walks near a Car, presses E to enter it, then holds W to drive forward. Verifies the enter-vehicle flow and that the Driven_Car moves.
tests.name: Player enters a car and drives it forward
source: // Find the nearest Car to the player and teleport the player right next to it.
harness.assert(cars.length > 0, 'There is at least one Car in the scene.');
const d = Math.hypot(c.centerX - getPlayer().centerX, c.centerY - getPlayer().centerY);
return d < best.dist ? { car: c, dist: d } : best;
// Place player right next to the car so the enter-range check passes.
harness.assert(getPlayer().hidden === false, 'Player is visible before entering the car.');
// Press E to enter the vehicle.
// After entering, the player should be hidden and a Driven_Car should exist.
harness.assert(playerAfterEnter.hidden === true, 'Player is hidden after entering the car.');
harness.assert(drivenCars.length > 0, 'A Driven_Car exists after entering the vehicle.');
const driveDist = Math.hypot(carAfter.centerX - carStart.centerX, carAfter.centerY - carStart.centerY);
harness.assert(driveDist > 30, 'Driven_Car moved forward while holding W (moved ' + driveDist.toFixed(1) + 'px).');
harness.assert(carAfter.behaviors.PhysicsCar3D.state.IsOnFloor === true, 'Driven_Car stays on the ground while driving.');

events.comment:
At each frame, the camera must catchup the target by a given ratio (speed)
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

The frame rate must not impact on the catch-up speed, we don't want a speed in ratio per frame but a speed ratio per second, like this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1s) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

Ok, but we still need to process each frame, we can use a exponent for this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * (1 - speed)^timeDelta
cameraX(t) = targetX + (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * exp(timeDelta * ln((1 - speed)))

pow is probably more efficient than precalculated log if the speed is changed continuously but this might be rare enough.

parameters: TargetedRotationAngle + 90 + RotationAngleOffset + AngleDifference(CameraAngle(Object.Layer()), TargetedRotationAngle + 90 + RotationAngleOffset) * exp(TimeDelta() * RotationLogSpeed)
TargetedElevationAngle + ElevationAngleOffset + AngleDifference(90 - Scene3D::CameraRotationX(Object.Layer()), TargetedElevationAngle + ElevationAngleOffset) * exp(TimeDelta() * ElevationLogSpeed)

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: SpriteMultitouchJoystick
description: Multitouch joysticks are objects showing a joystick on the screen, useful for mobile. They work like a physical gamepad:

- Automatic "mapper" behaviors for 2D and 3D movement behaviors (platformer characters, top-down movement, 3D character etc...). Add one of these to the object with the movement behavior (i.e: the player most of the time) and the behavior will then be controlled automatically by the virtual joystick (it works by reading the multitouch joystick state and simulating controls). No need for additional events to make it work once the behaviors are set up.
There are ready-to-use joysticks in the asset-store [multitouch joysticks pack](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?initial-dialog=asset-store&asset-pack=multitouch-joysticks-multitouch-joysticks).

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: MousePointerLock
eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: Lock and hide mouse pointer for unlimited movement (e.g., FPS mouse look).
description: This behavior removes the limit on the distance the mouse can move and hides the cursor.
For example, a user can rotate or continue to manipulate an object by moving the mouse endlessly ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://mouse-pointer-lock)).
Without the pointer lock, the rotation or operation will stop the moment the pointer reaches the edge of the browser or screen.
Game players don't have to worry about leaving the gameplay area or accidentally clicking on another application that moves the mouse focus away from the game.
Locking the pointer locks `CursorX()` and `CursorY()` expressions.
